utterances.text: In the stills book, as I mentioned, there's a couple of pages that will be a little bit out of order perhaps from the video. In terms of the video, with the knowledge that everyone had, they did try to make it chronological. There are some of the days you'll notice in the video and in the stills book where, you know, we don't know if it's for sure July 10th or July 11th and that's noted. So it's possible that there could be, you know, a mistake made on one of those two days, but the best of our knowledge, the best of the knowledge of the team at that time and based off of testimony reports, et cetera, they've tried to make it chronological.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, if I can ask Ms. Stewart, we will get ready to start the video, but before we do -- of course, she's ready to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you just give us a little preview of what we are going to see in the opening shots of the video?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: As the video starts, you'll see some motorised artillery moving down the road. That's mainly it, you'll see Pragas, tanks, et cetera, moving on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And for the Registry, we'll be starting with the stills book which was P624 and the first still will be -- should be number 5. E-court number -- page 5 in that, but we'll first --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before we deal with the documents, the stills and the video, there are some questions I would like to ask you, Mr. McCloskey. Sometimes when we have seen videos, we saw subtitles in English, the original text we could hear was in B/C/S, and we had problems with translation into French and so on. Could you explain if there are transcripts of the videos, of the text, in B/C/S, in English, in French, so that we can follow better and we have understanding about the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. The transcript is P1008. That should be in B/C/S and English. I don't know if we've done it in French so I don't think there is a French transcript, but of course, we can send that to CLSS and have that in French.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In that case we will not have a translation, actual translation today into French. Just you should bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Because there's no interpretation directly from the video, as we have learned recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, we normally prefer that you hear the language and the tone, though this does create a problem because not only do we, of course, want French for you to hear, there needs to be a French archives for this Tribunal and so that's -- normally the interpreters will speak over the -- basically reading out the subtitles and then that gets translated into French and that can be done if you prefer. And it's just -- the interpreters have been very flexible on this point, but like you've said, if there's not a French transcript, it may be difficult. But sometimes they've been able to manage with -- but I guess we'll just have to see how it goes. But we, of course, can have them read the subtitles and then that gets translated, if you would like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But we are in the hands of the interpreters. We all are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And there's something else Judge Nyambe wants to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: I have a clarification I would like from the witness for my better understanding of the proceedings. You, in line -- page 38, line 10 to 13, you referred to reviewing of videos and still book and also somewhere else you referred to editing of video footages. Have I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I must have misspoken. I certainly didn't edit any of the video footage myself. That would have been the film-maker. I reviewed the footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Then I'll try to rephrase my question again. Do you have an understanding of what editing of a video entails exactly? What do you achieve at the end of the process?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do, having done a little bit of video editing work myself prior to becoming -- prior going to graduate school. It is looking at a lot of different footage, raw footage, choosing which sections you would like to make -- to become a part of the, let's say, the trial video, and cutting out those sections, whether it's actually splicing in film with actual film or the old video machines or computers these days, but selecting those sections, putting them into the new video. And you can intersperse those sections, those edits, all throughout the course of the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: So it is my understanding then that in the process of editing of video, you can leave some materials or you can add some materials?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I have another question for you. At page 38, lines 10 to 13, and please correct me if I don't quote you correctly, I've got you saying: "When I have been reviewing the book and reviewing the video, I'm not seeing some things that I think should be changed, we think should be changed and some corrections. There are some small mistakes in it as well." Can you just explain to me exactly what that means, what you mean to say there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sure. And I am pretty much exclusively just talking about the stills book. As I've been reviewing it, I've noticed a couple of small mistakes or some changes to make it more complete. For example, even on this first page here where it says "Reuters footage," I know that some of this footage is also from WTN as well as Reuters. It's a bit detailed but I would put WTN and Reuters. There'll be a page that comes up later where it is the wrong video that was cited and I would choose to put in the correct video since I've been able to find which one that is. In the book, I would also add in where there's been more testimony that has identified where people have identified individuals in the book. This book, as I said, was made in 2003 for an older trial, Blagojevic and Jokic. It has remained pretty much the same and though there have been additions added to it, but it hasn't been completed since partway through the last trial, so there's more testimony that can be added to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And let me add a bit to that. When you say that it was material that was actually edited out, sort of left on the cutting-room floor, do you know, from speaking to Ms. Fracassetti and your knowledge of an investigation, why something would have been edited out generally?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Yeah, both in speaking with Marta Fracassetti as well as viewing the original raw footage myself, the times that anything has been edited out either it's -- it's, let's say, duplicative, it exists in other versions so no need to put in several versions of SRT's footage. Sometimes it's just it might not be very good quality and there may be a choice of something that's better quality. And sometimes it's just too much footage, we don't need to see, you know 20 minutes of something when a couple of minutes shows the exact same story, the same point. So those are the main reasons why anything was left out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recall were there any specific areas of the film where Ms. Fracassetti received instructions not to leave anything out but just to put in the whole collection of what the Prosecutor had?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Yes. She told me that she had kept everything related to the VRS in Srebrenica, so to have everything from that that exists to be put into the video, as well as all existing footage from the Hotel Fontana meetings, those three meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And can you recall -- can you give us an example of the kind of thing where she would have done significant editing and leaving, you know, material out that may have just been too long, as you've said?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: I know one example is the individual who gave us the footage on the -- about the column. And it's not long footage but it's too long to put into the trial video, and it's -- what you see is what exists there, it's just more of the same thing for another, you know, 10 minutes or so. So she's just taken you know, a couple of minutes of that and put that into the trial video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, for your knowledge, we have not offered all the raw footage for you, but we have provided all the raw footage to the Defence, so they have all of that material. And of course, we can provide any raw footage that you would like.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Another question, you mentioned the old-fashioned splicing of tape or film. Do you know what -- the basic technology that Ms. Fracassetti used?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what machines she used. I know she referred to doing the rough edit on the videotape machines and doing the final edit using -- now using the computer systems, so you can download the video, let's say, the rough edit of the video on to the computer and then make more exact -- exact edits on the computer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And have you, to help explain this process, set out or retrieved some two video segments to try to illustrate how this was done?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Correct. You'll see later there's some raw footage of an interview with General Mladic and you'll see the complete footage from the two different original sources. And then you'll see what is in the trial video, which is the edited version of that video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So we'll get into a little more detail about how -- when we get to that section. All right. Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe would like to put a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: I just want a clarification. Just now you've said "raw footage," does that imply there is another kind of footage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'll use the term "original footage," so the footage that Marta Fracassetti used to make the trial video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, since we have e-court page 5 of P624 up on the screen, we might as well have you discuss that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we blow it up one more time, just for my eyes. If we could go down a little bit so we can see the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Can you -- we see it says "Zvornik Brigade Praga self-propelled anti-aircraft gun." How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: If you -- well, if you read further you'll see that there is a registration number associated with the Praga. If you look at the Praga and you see the bicycle ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you look at the Praga, you see the bicycle and go to the left over the tire, you'll see a number, licence plate number. And if it were a little brighter, yeah, you can see that it's 11067.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I can't make that out on this still myself. Is there any other way to do it?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Yes, actually in the -- we have the luxury of seeing the video where we can get -- we are able to view it moving a little bit closer and can freeze it a little bit better so the numbers are a little more clearer than this particular photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So were you able to do that or the team able to do that to determine these numbers?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Right. So the team did that and was able to get the registration number of the 11067. And we have a vehicle log from the Zvornik Brigade that was seized from the Zvornik Brigade in 1998, and in the original vehicle log it shows that there is a Praga with that registration number that is part of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I apologise if we've gone over this, but can you tell the Court a little bit about the seizure from the Zvornik Brigade. When that occurred, what that was about, just briefly? If you know.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: It was in March of 1998. There was a team actually split up into two teams of investigators and analysts that went to both the Zvornik Brigade and the Bratunac Brigade and seized numerous documents from both brigades, and as part of the collection of those documents were quite a few vehicle logs which this vehicle log was found.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how did you use the vehicle log to identify this machine?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: On the vehicle log itself it shows the registration number, it shows the Praga, it shows that it's a Praga, it shows it's from the Zvornik Brigade and there's more information as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to that, 06595 is the number I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do we have the originals? If anyone would like to see the originals, we have them. We won't be doing this for every exhibit but we thought we would start off to give you a feel for this. And if we could get that up on the screen, that's 65 ter, we can get an idea. All right. If we could -- I think we need to blow up the left side. I'm not sure initially -- sorry, not that side but the other side of the B/C/S document. I'm not sure we absolutely have to have the English but, yes, that's very helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So is this the information you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And so we see that in the second line it -- well, we have a date, 1 July through 31 July 1995. It says "Type, Praga." And then number 11067. Now, aside from this identification from the Zvornik Brigade, does this document give us any idea where this machine was in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Yes. If you go to the next page, you'll see the routes designated on certain days.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I think we are really going to need to blow up the -- well, the English at first, if we could, so we can look in the period of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, I note that your still book at the bottom says under "Location": "On the road just south of Srebrenica, 10th or 11 July 1995." So what do you gain from this document in putting together this information in the stills book?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: It also helps to confirm or corroborate that this Praga was in this area at that time. If you look at the July 9th route, it shows Pribicevac, Zeleni Jadar and Zivkovo Brdo. And then on the 10th and 11th, worked in those positions and then the same the day after.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. I see it says "Z. Brdo." Why did you say Zivko -- I am sorry, I can't pronounce that, Zivkovo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Zivkovo Brdo. Well, you'll actually see another vehicle log where it is, there's tank that actually spells it out, that it's in that pro location. We also know from actually testimony from witnesses prior that placed their units themselves in that location prior to the entry into Srebrenica on the 11th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you just remind us very generally, where Pribicevac, Zeleni Jadar, and this Zivkovo Brdo are?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: They are south of Srebrenica. Zeleni Jadar is -- all the locations are south of Srebrenica. Zivkovo Brdo is maybe halfway between Zeleni Jadar and Srebrenica. It's north of it, north-west of it. It's an elevated area, it's a hill area. And Pribicevac is north and east of that, and that's where the forward command post was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And I won't put that up, but are all these three listed on the map in the map book?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go back to the still photograph, if we could, number 5 of 624. Actually, let's just leave it there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, are you tendering this log-book? Or at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's one of those ones that we picked up in preparation for this to help you provide detail that did not believe have a 65 ter number, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It has --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- I can't offer it. I mean, it's got a -- one that we gave it so it could be used in court and we provided it to the Defence and they didn't have any problem. I can offer that into evidence as a helpful guide to this material. The Defence has had it for a while, they understood that we were going to do this and I heard no objection from them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But in the lists of documents you intend to use with the witness, there are many which are not yet on the 65 ter exhibit list. All those with a star, you had a 65 ter number. This is one of them, and therefore I don't know how to -- you want to proceed to give the accused a chance to give his comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, those video stills are taken right off the video, so I don't know how technical we want to get with 65 ter numbers, but they are -- the 65 ter number is the video itself, that frame is on the video. So it does in that sense have a 65 ter number, but for the simple sense that we'd freeze it and that would be something that we could relate to, we've given it a new number. This is different, this particular one we just -- it's mentioned in the stills book. It's cited in the stills book. So in some sense, its 65 ter number would be the stills book number where it's cited. As you know, 65 ter is made -- put the Defence and everyone on notice, so notice really isn't an issue because this log is cited as historically part of the record forever. They haven't objected reasonably and so I could argue that this is a 65 ter number, but fundamentally, it's better to give it a new one for the record. And I think that's probably the story with all of these. They are just a different format of something that already has a 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: At a later stage we have to identify the documents. And you have in the list of documents to be used with this witness two documents, Zvornik Brigade vehicle log number 22, and then the same number but related to different vehicles. This is 65 ter 06594 and 5. And now we have on the screen the number with 5 at the end. But, I think I would like to know Mr. Gajic's or, respectively, the Defence position on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just a remark. I will, of course, give my response once I've consulted Mr. Tolimir. Firstly, Mr. McCloskey said twice that the Defence did not oppose it or make an objection. Well, just to make the record clear, the Defence has not had an opportunity to speak their mind on this yet, so I want to make that clear. This is a different matter altogether.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey. Oh, you want to add something, Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as this specific document is concerned, the Defence do not oppose its admission into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: First, it will be added to the 65 ter exhibit list with the leave of the Chamber and admitted into evidence. This specific document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the two-page document under 65 ter 06595 will be assigned Exhibit P01128.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this brings up a -- just another issue. If I -- it would be very helpful, as it would be in any trial in any country, for the parties to know when there are objections to materials as soon in advance as possible because it's impossible to predict. If we went through every iota of detail on every document we had, we would be here for ten years, and they have been very reasonable in not objecting to material that is very clear and has been open to them for a long time, but I'm a little concerned about not hearing about objections until we are halfway there. In many jurisdictions, if a party is going to move that evidence be withdrawn or not be used, suppressed, it's incumbent to do that before the trial. We don't have that rule here, but if we could just -- if the Defence could work on providing us with notice on that as soon as possible, that would just help everyone quite a bit. They can absolutely -- don't have to take a position ever. It's our burden, of course. But in this adversarial hybrid system, that would be very helpful, and I would appreciate that, thank you. I think I've probably talked our way into the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, of course the Prosecution have always put us on notice of matters, sometimes earlier, sometimes later. But let's make one thing clear, the material that is not officially listed on the 65 ter list evidently is a sort of material the Prosecution did not intend use, at least not within the foreseeable future. And I believe that the Chamber has given clear guidance, both to the Prosecution and the Defence, on the use of material and the handling of material. I think the Prosecution was specifically told what the guidance was with regard to the material that can be put on the 65 ter list. Of course, where the material is not that relevant or important, the Defence will not object. In other cases, however, there are matters that pose great difficulties for us because there is a great amount of non-disclosed [as interpreted] material, and it is physically impossible ever since the pre-trial stage to date to even go through all the materials. So we request that if the Prosecution intend to use certain documents, to notify us reasonably in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm a little bit concerned that we have this discussion now because I thought that we have resolved this problem already at an earlier stage in this trial, and I, in fact, don't see any conflict or any problem up to now. I think the way the parties gave notice to each other was very well maintained, and therefore, I think we should leave it like it is and look that we have a fair trial. And of course, sometimes it's last-minute notice. We received three different versions of the documents the Prosecution intends to use since yesterday, so that happens and will happen by the other party as well. We are not concerned about that. We are sure that everybody is aware of the procedure and we will avoid any problems in this respect. We have now the time for the second break, indeed, and we will resume 10 minutes before 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just one correction on page 59, line 20. It seems to be a case of misinterpretation because I didn't say non-disclosed material, I said there is a great amount of disclosed material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Indeed this is a big difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And second, I would like to clarify, the Defence has always been very flexible as far as adding to the 65 ter list is concerned and this is clear from our practice until now, and we always state our position as to whether we accept something or not. I would just appreciate it if the Prosecutor would refrain from stating our position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes. I think everybody can -- you are in the position to make your position very clear by your -- that's acceptable. And I think there is no concern about the disclosure procedure any longer because there is no concern by the Defence. Mr. McCloskey, go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, could we blow this up a little -- I mean, make it so it's smaller so we can see the dates on this -- the document that's on the screen now. It's the vehicle log 1128. So we can just see the dates there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I notice in your still book of this Praga, at the bottom it says: "South of Srebrenica -- on the road just south of Srebrenica, 10 or 11 July." How is it that it's only 10 or 11 July?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Well, it's a combination of different things. Partly from the vehicle log you see that there in that area of certainly July 9th, 10th, 11th. You'll see another vehicle log that will pin-point it a little bit more. It's consistent of where we know units were at, where people have testified where the Zvornik Brigade is located on the 10th or 11th, before entering Srebrenica on July 11th. Also from testimony and documents, there was fighting in this area on July 9th and also again on the morning of July 10th before the Zvornik Brigade and VRS take this area, and the road is clear to proceed into Srebrenica. So it's a combination of logs, of testimony, knowledge of events that pin-points it during those several days but we are not able to say exactly whether it's the afternoon of the 10th or the morning of the 11th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Let's actually continue playing the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Would you please state for the record the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, this will be P991, and when I say "the video," it will be the same video each time. And the still book will be P624 each time. Yeah, if we could just play it and try to stop it at the Praga, similar to where the stills book is. It doesn't need to be exact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Is this roughly the footage that the still was taken from?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And for the record it's 00.23.8. All right, let's continue to play the trial video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's go to the stills book, P624. We note for the record we are now stopped at 32.4 on the counter. The stills book, 624, e-court page 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, can you just briefly explain this?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: As you just saw in the video where it stopped, this is a tank and you can see once again there's registration number similar to what you saw on the Praga. Now this time it is above, if you see where the driver is, his head, there's a four-digit number right above his head on the right side. It says "6717." And similar to the Praga, it is also a Zvornik Brigade tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, all right, if we could go to 65 ter 6594.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And just again, how does this exhibit, as it's coming up, relate to the tank on the screen?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Similar to what you saw with the Praga, you have the date, you have that it's a tank, T-55, with the registration number of 6717, as being a vehicle, part of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sorry, we want the other -- the right side of both documents. Thank you. All right. If we could go to the next page in both documents. And if we could below it up a little bit so we can see 9, 10, 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we had talked briefly about -- I'd ask you how you knew it was Zivkovo Brdo. Does this document help you sort that out, because in the last document I think it just said "Z. Brdo"?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Yes, it is one of the means that helped sort that out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Where do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: You'll see it on the July 8th row of where the -- the route of where the tank was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And this area, Bojna, that we see on the 11th, do you know where that is?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: That's south of Srebrenica, on the road to Srebrenica. A little bit, it would be east and north of Zivkovo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And is your explanation on why we say 10 or 11 the same as the last exhibit?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. We'd offer this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the two-page document under 65 ter number 06594 will be assigned Exhibit P01129.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would kindly ask, when a question is being put, not to ask, Is your answer going to be identical to your previous answers, because that is suggesting what the witness should say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, that was my impression as well. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't think it suggests the answer, it could be either way. It could be yes or no. And I'm obviously just trying to save some time, but I don't believe it's a leading question. But if the Court rules it is, I won't do that again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I didn't rule on that, I told you my observation. Perhaps you just be careful. Sometimes Mr. Tolimir is objecting to some questions which could appear to be a leading question but it depends, of course, on the capability of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, some questions can be leading and be appropriate for the Court for the very reason, to save some time, that it's nothing that is going to cause any problem or any issues for anyone. I'd like to know what the particular problem is in such a question, because if it's a problem I won't do it, but it seems to me it's an objection for the sake of objecting and it's absurd in the context of this case to be objecting like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Except the word "absurd," I would agree with you. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I think we can just continue to play the video. Of course, if anyone has any questions, otherwise, I think I'll just let it play. We don't, as she said, don't have stills for every part of the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could go to stills book 624. And we are now at 55.2. And it's e-court page 7. If we could put that up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We can see that this says "Colonel Vinko Pandurevic, commander of the Zvornik Brigade." And how can you come to that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: A couple of ways. One of them is that Lieutenant-Colonel Pandurevic identified himself when he testified, January 29th, 2009. It was not this exact still but it was shortly thereafter in a nearby location on the approach to Srebrenica. As well as I'm familiar with him just over the years of the course of our investigation and having been a part of the trial, where I saw him in trial for the last three years.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You might want to try a talk a little slower just -- I know it's difficult to get the rhythm, but -- all right. And it says, "Location: South of Srebrenica, 10 or 11 July." Do you know any more than south of Srebrenica? Have you figured out exactly where this is?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: I don't know exactly where it is. No, I can't tell you exactly where it is other than south of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how do you conclude that it's south of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: It's going to be from certainly prior testimony of people that were in the area such as Lieutenant-Colonel Pandurevic, once again from combat reports, situation reports, where we know roughly where units are, and we know in particular that his unit was fighting for that elevation I mentioned of Zivkovo Brdo, on the 9th and again on the 10th. So we believe that he is near this location, but don't know exactly on those dates before entering Srebrenica on July 11th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's just continue to play the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. We are at 1.13.4.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you have any idea who is taking this video?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's just continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now at the trial video we are at 1.38.4. We've changed scenes and we have an image in front of us. Can you tell us what this is?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: This is -- this is Major Milan Jolovic, he has the nickname of Legenda, speaking into the radio, obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And let's go to the stills book, P24, e-court page 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is this roughly the same image as we've had on the screen, unfortunately not as good quality?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And how were you able to make this conclusion that this is Legenda or Milan Jolovic?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Well, as you see, as noted on the still there, that he was identified by Colonel Mirko Trivic in the Popovic trial, and I can give you the date on that, that's May 21st, 2007. In addition, he was also identified by Lieutenant-Colonel Vinko Pandurevic in the Popovic trial when he testified himself on January 29th, 2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you just tell us the unit Colonel Trivic belonged to?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: He was commander of the 2nd Romanija Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can he be seen on any of the Srebrenica videos?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: You will see him coming up shortly in the town of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. We see down at: "On the road south of Srebrenica, 10 or 11 July." Do you have anything to add to your explanation about how those conclusions were made?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Right. In the testimony of Lieutenant-Colonel Vinko Pandurevic, he testified that Major Jolovic was in this area, he believed to be in the, once again, Zivkovo Brdo area overlooking Pusmulici village, trying to -- egging his troops on and that he believed that to be on July 10th during the counter-attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you tell us what you think this lettering up in the right-hand corner, I think we all know at this point that eight-digit number is an ERN; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm talking about right underneath that, what is that that we can see? It's sort of a pinkish-brown, blackish colour?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: In Cyrillic that's "SRT," which is Srpska Radio Television, and as I mentioned, that they had broadcast some of this footage on this station. And so you will see the "SRT" in some of this footage in the trial video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. If we can continue playing P991, the trial video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, I didn't turn on my microphone. Since this goes to identification on a photograph, sometimes it is claimed that somebody was in a certain place on the 10th or on the 11th, and we have evidence that Vinko Pandurevic was somewhere on the 10th or 11th, can we see from this footage whether this still was made in a certain place at a certain time? If an assertion is just made that Legenda was in such and such a place on the 10th or the 11th, I don't think that's acceptable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think the sources cited by Ms. Gallagher are fine. Vinko Pandurevic testified, as she said, in his own case and can confirm this. You will be able to see the video and at this point with the purpose of this witness, this is perfectly appropriate and fine. I don't know what else the General is suggesting we do at this point, but through this witness she has provided the basics that the investigation has and I think it's perfectly appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Chamber doesn't give any weight to these documents at this stage of our proceedings. We will come to that later when we are in the position to give weight to all evidence before the Chamber. It's not a -- if we can believe it or not, we don't know yet. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, just logistically, I think I will be offering all of these images into evidence. I could do it as we go, but it's part of one exhibit, so I think it would be better if I just waited at this point. If we could just continue to play the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you hear any location in that audio?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Other than the reference to a bridge, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: And also "down there," hinting at their -- at an elevation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I apologise, let's just keep running it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. We are now at 2.33.1 and we have this SRT logo and there's some Serbian overlay to this. What can you tell us about this? It's clearly different. We now have this overlay of somebody speaking. Do you know what that is?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: It appears to be a newscast from SRT.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And these shots from this newscast, where do you think they are from, and what locations do you think they are filming?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Once again, I think it's going to be roughly the same location south of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is it possible they have pulled this from some archival footage and it's not Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Well, it's consistent with testimony that we've heard who -- from people that have been in the area that it is still south of Srebrenica during the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Have you or the investigators been able to make any identifications from this film that we are seeing to actual areas?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: In terms of this part of the film, no, I couldn't say exactly where it is along the road, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's just continue to play, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know when and where this footage at 3.10.7 that -- of men in uniform with blue helmets is?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's keep going.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. We've come to about 4.50.1, was entitled "Muslim footage Srebrenica." I believe it said 10 July. What can you tell us about the source of this footage that we are about to see?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: This is -- the source is from --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And could we go, I am sorry, could we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in public session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And if we could just --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: One other question, is there some shots in an apartment?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: That's correct. You will see a little bit shot of inside his apartment and his family.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Has there been any editing at that point for any reason regarding people's faces?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Yes. They are blocked out by -- not by him, it's not in the original footage, so it's by our team.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And why was that done?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: To protect their confidentiality, their identity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I think we can play it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We are at 06.12.1 and we see some men in uniform. And do you know, has the investigation determined what unit this is, or what army?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Well, I assume it's the BiH Muslim Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just briefly, what is this?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: That's the UN base in Srebrenica, Bravo Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: At 6.43.3. Okay. We can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just for the record, we now for the first time at approximately 7.29.8, perhaps a second or two before that, we now see some numbers on the left. What are those numbers?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: It's the date, July 10th, 1995, and the time of 20 hours, 11 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Does the person who provided this video identify anyone in this frame at 8.42.9?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: He states in his statement that Ramiz Becirovic spoke to the people in Srebrenica. I don't know if this -- my assumption is that this is who he is. I can't identify him myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's just continue, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And just for the record, we've now gone to what is marked as 11 July in the time stamp and we are at 10.19.9. If we could continue to play it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now at 13.57.9 we've clearly changed from the crowded down-town area to somewhere else. Does the provider of this provide any information on where this is or what it is that we are seeing now?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: Yeah, he noted in his statement that at 14.37 he took footage of the men leaving the enclave and walking towards Susnjari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's continue to play. We'll stop pretty soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. We are now stopping for the day at 14.53.2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That last section of footage, does he provide anything in his statement about where that is?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER
utterances.text: No, nothing more than it was the approach to Susnjari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Then I think this is a good place to stop. And Mr. President, I hope you got the word, but this was meant as a -- as to take up our day because this is, it's a lot of video so it's good to break it up and as a good person to -- as the gap filler, we need to start tomorrow morning with the witness as scheduled who is here and will be ready to go, the other witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. As you perhaps know, during the break, and you will be here -- before you will be here again, you are not allowed to contact the parties about the content of your testimony, although you are an investigator of the OTP, you should work with your colleagues of course. We have to adjourn now and you will be called at another day in this trial. We resume tomorrow morning at 9.00 in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
